title: Modelling orthographic similarity effects in recognition memory reveals support for open bigram representations of letter coding; Modeling the continuous recognition paradigm to determine how retrieval can impact subsequent retrievals
authors: Lyulei Zhang, Adam F. Osth; Julian Fox, Adam F. Osth
caption_short: Schematic of the two paradigms: (A) study-test lists whose new test items are made by swapping or replacing letters of studied words or nonwords; (B) continuous recognition, in which every word in a long stream is judged as seen before or new.
notes: Drawn by us: neither paper has a procedure figure (Zhang & Osth Figure 1 illustrates letter-coding schemes; Fox & Osth Figure 1 illustrates sources of interference; the other figures show model mechanisms or results). Both articles are open access under CC BY 4.0 (Crossref licence record); the preprints used for checking are PsyArXiv 95hnw and 7dhz3 (CC BY 4.0). Panel A follows Zhang & Osth preprint pp. 17-21 (33 study words, 89 test probes, 1 s per word, 45 s maths distractor); COLD / CLOD is the transposition example used in the paper's text, TRIAL / TRAIL is ours. Panel B follows Fox & Osth preprint pp. 17-19 (lists of 360 trials, lags 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16, 24, 32 or 40 intervening trials); the preprint describes only one experiment, so the second continuous-recognition file (Experiment 2) could not be checked against text. Rendered with Pillow (scripts/schem_words.py).
